blocks.text: [1] [^n2515]And Jesus said, To judge the world am I come, so that they that see not may [2] see, and they that see may become blind. [^n2516]And some of the Pharisees which were [3] with him heard that, and they said unto him, Can it be that we are blind? [^n2517]Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye should not have sin: but now ye say, We see: and because of this your sin remaineth.[^n2518]

[4] [Arabic, p. 140] [^n2519]Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever entereth not into the fold of the sheep by the door, but goeth up from another place, that man is a thief and a [5, 6] stealer. [^n2520]But he that entereth by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. [^n2521]And therefore[^n2522] the keeper of the door openeth for him the door; and the sheep hear his voice: and [7] he calleth his sheep[^n2523] by their names, and they go forth unto him. [^n2524]And when he putteth forth his sheep, he goeth before them, and his sheep[^n2525] follow him: because [8] they know his voice. [^n2526]And after a stranger will the sheep not go, but they flee from [9] him: because they hear not the voice of a stranger. [^n2527]This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they knew not what he was saying unto them.

[10] [^n2528]Jesus said unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the [11] sheep. [^n2529]And all that came are thieves and stealers: but the sheep heard them not. [12] [^n2530]I am the door: and if a man enter by me, he shall live, and shall go in and go out, [13] and shall find pasture. [^n2531]And the stealer cometh not, save that he may steal, and kill, and destroy: but I came that they might have life, and that they might have [14] the thing that is better.[^n2532] [^n2533]I am the good shepherd; and the good shepherd giveth [15] himself[^n2534] for his sheep. [^n2535]But the hireling, who is not a shepherd, and whose the sheep[^n2536] are not, when he seeth the wolf as it cometh, leaveth the sheep, and fleeth, [16] and the wolf cometh, and snatcheth away the sheep, and scattereth[^n2537] them: [^n2538]and the [17] hireling fleeth because he is an hireling, and hath no care for the sheep. [^n2539]I am the [18] good shepherd; [^n2540]and I know what is mine, and what is mine knoweth me, as my Father knoweth me, and I know my Father; and I give myself[^n2541] for the sheep. [19] [^n2542]And I have other sheep also, that are not of this flock: them also I must invite, and they shall hear my voice; and all the sheep shall be one, and the shepherd one. [20] [Arabic, p. 141] [^n2543]And therefore doth my Father love me, because I give my life, that I may [21] take it again. [^n2544]No man taketh it from me, but I leave it of my own choice. And I have the right to leave it, and have the right also to take it. And this commandment did I receive of my Father.

[22] [^n2545]And there occurred a disagreement among the Jews because of these sayings. [23] [^n2546]And many of them said, He hath a devil, and is afflicted with madness;[^n2547] why listen [24] ye to him? [^n2548]And others said, These sayings are not those of men possessed with demons. Can a demon haply open the eyes of a blind man?

[25, 26] [^n2549]And the feast of the dedication came on at Jerusalem: and it was winter. [^n2550]And [27] Jesus was walking in the temple in the porch of Solomon. [^n2551]The Jews therefore surrounded him, and said unto him, Until when dost thou make our hearts anxious? [28] [^n2552]If thou art the Messiah, tell us plainly. He answered and said unto them, I told you, and ye believe not: and the deeds that I do in my Father’s name bear witness [29, 30] to me. [^n2553]But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep,[^n2554] as I said unto you. [31] [^n2555]And my sheep[^n2556] hear my voice, and I know them, and they come after me: [^n2557]and I give them eternal life; and they shall not perish for ever, nor shall any man snatch [32] them out of my hands.[^n2558] [^n2559]For the Father, who hath given them unto me, is greater [33] than all; and no man is able to take them from the hand of my[^n2560] Father. [^n2561]I and [34, 35] my Father are one. [^n2562]And the Jews took stones to stone him. [^n2563]Jesus said unto them, Many good deeds from my Father have I shewed you; because of which[^n2564] of them, [36] then, do ye stone me? [^n2565]The Jews said unto him, Not for the good deeds do we stone thee, but because thou blasphemest; and, whilst thou art a man, makest thyself [37] God. [^n2566]Jesus said unto them, Is it not thus written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? [38] [Arabic, p. 142] [^n2567]And if he called those gods—for[^n2568] to them came the word of God (and it is [39] not possible in[^n2569] the scripture that anything should be undone)—[^n2570]he then, whom the Father hath sanctified and sent into the world, do ye say that he blasphemeth; [40] because I said unto you, I am the Son of God? [^n2571]If then I do not the deeds of my [41] Father, ye believe me not.[^n2572] [^n2573]But if I do, even if ye believe not me, believe the deeds: that ye may know and believe that my Father is in me, and I in my Father. [42] [^n2574]And they sought again to take him: and he went forth out of their hands.

[43] [^n2575]And he went beyond Jordan to the place where John was baptizing formerly; [44] and abode there. [^n2576]And many people came unto him; and they said, John did not [45] work even one sign: but all that John said of this man is truth. [^n2577]And many believed in him.

[46] [^n2578]And there was a sick man, named Lazarus, of the village of Bethany, the brother [47] of Mary and Martha. [^n2579]And Mary was she that anointed with sweet ointment the feet of Jesus, and wiped them with her hair; and Lazarus, who was sick, was the [48] brother of this woman.[^n2580] [^n2581]And his sisters sent unto Jesus, and said unto him, Our [49] Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick. [^n2582]But Jesus said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glorifying of God, that the Son of God may be glorified [50, 51] because of it. [^n2583]And Jesus loved Martha, and Mary, and Lazarus. [^n2584]And when he [52] heard that he was sick, he abode in the place where he was two days. [^n2585]And after that, [53] he said unto his disciples, Come, let us go into Judæa. [^n2586]His disciples said unto him, Our [Arabic, p. 143] Master, now the Jews desire to stone thee; and goest thou again thither? [54, 55] [^n2587]Jesus said unto them, Is not the day of twelve hours? If then a man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of the world. [^n2588]But if [56] a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because there is no lamp in him. [^n2589]This said Jesus: and after that, he said unto them, Lazarus our friend hath fallen asleep; but [57] I am going to awaken him. [^n2590]His disciples said unto him, Our Lord, if he hath [58] fallen asleep, he will recover. [^n2591]But Jesus said that concerning his death: while they [59] supposed that he spake of lying down to sleep. [^n2592]Then Jesus said unto them plainly, [60] Lazarus is dead. [^n2593]And I am glad that I was not there for your sakes, that ye may [61] believe; but let us go thither. [^n2594]Thomas, who is called Thama,[^n2595] said to the disciples, his companions, Let us also go, and die with him.

n2523.text: A different word (lit. rams) from that used in the other verses; so in Peshitta (cf. Sin., which, however, differs somewhat); cf. also § 54, 40 f., note.

n2525.text: A different word (lit. rams) from that used in the other verses; so in Peshitta (cf. Sin., which, however, differs somewhat); cf. also § 54, 40 f., note.

n2532.text: Or, best thing. Vat. ms. omits from but I came.

n2558.text: Or, hand; but probably dual (cf. Syr.).

n2560.text: So Peshitta; but Sin. the. Borg. ms. omits the hand of.

n2569.text: This in could more easily arise as a clerical error (repetition) in the Syriac text.

n2572.text: So Ciasca’s text, following Vat. ms. But this is probably a clerical error for the reading of Borg. ms., which omits ye.
